youtube.title: Why Is a Year Not Exactly 365 Days? #Shorts
youtube.description: We think a year is 365 days. It isn't. From one spring to the next the Earth takes about 365 days, 5 hours and 49 minutes, leaving almost a quarter of a day over every year. The leap year fixed that with one extra day every fourth year, but it overcorrected by about eleven minutes. Over sixteen centuries, that added up to ten whole days. Full episode on the channel. #Shorts #leapyear #calendar #science #thehiddenwhy
tags: why is a year not 365 days

instagram.caption: A year isn't 365 days. It's 365 days, 5 hours and 49 minutes, so a quarter of a day is left over every year. Leap years fix it, but the first fix was eleven minutes too long and added up to ten days. Follow for more hidden whys. #thehiddenwhy #leapyear #science #calendar
